concepts.name: Market Structure
concepts.definition: Framework for reading swing highs, swing lows and directional sequences. The playbook uses higher-timeframe structure for context before lower-timeframe execution.
howToUse: Mark meaningful confirmed Monthly/Weekly/Daily swings.

tutorials.title: Build a Higher-Timeframe Structure Map
tutorials.objective: Create a repeatable structure map using confirmed swings, continuation breaks and potential shifts.
materials: One completed futures chart with at least Daily, 1H and 5M views
A written swing and candle-close rule
A replay or screenshot tool
steps: Choose one instrument and one completed date. Record the contract/continuous symbol, expiry convention, chart feed and timezone.
On Daily and 1H, mark only swings that satisfy one preselected pivot rule. Do not use a future-known turning point before it is confirmed.
Identify the latest relevant break. Label BOS only when the predeclared level and wick/body rule are met.
If studying a possible reversal, record the prior short-term swing, the opposing break and whether displacement accompanies it. Keep MSS distinct from a continuation BOS.
Move to 5M only after the higher-timeframe map is saved. Record what lower-timeframe information refines the map and what does not change it.
tutorials.deliverable: A three-timeframe chart pack with five annotated pivots, one candidate BOS/MSS decision and a written invalidation/no-trade note.
review: Pivot rule is stated before marking.
BOS and MSS are not used interchangeably.
The lower timeframe does not retroactively rewrite the higher-timeframe swing map.

tutorials.title: Create a Liquidity Reference Ledger
tutorials.objective: Map potential buy-side/sell-side objectives and distinguish a reference level from an entry trigger.
materials: A completed NQ, ES, GC or CL session chart
A fixed definition of trading day/week and session timezone
A spreadsheet or journal
steps: Before reviewing the outcome, record the product, expiry, data feed, timezone and session definition.
Mark the last completed day and week highs/lows, plus the chosen session high/low.
Mark equal-high/equal-low clusters using a tolerance fixed in ticks or points before reviewing the move.
Label potential BSL above highs and SSL below lows. Describe these as chart-based hypotheses, not visible orders or measured resting liquidity.
Choose one possible opposing pool as an objective and record what separate trigger would be required before a trade could be considered.
tutorials.deliverable: A dated liquidity ledger with at least six premarked pools, tolerance/session rules and a separate trigger column.
review: Levels were marked before studying the later move.
Exchange trading day is not confused with calendar midnight.
No assumption that every pool must be taken.

tutorials.title: Separate a Liquidity Sweep from Breakout Acceptance
tutorials.objective: Classify level interactions using a consistent reclaim/acceptance rule instead of hindsight labels.
materials: At least ten completed level interactions
A chosen wick/body close rule
A chart replay tool
steps: Select ten prior-day, prior-week, equal-high/low or session levels and mark them before replay.
For every interaction, record whether price traded beyond the level, reclaimed it, closed back inside, or held outside with follow-through.
Apply the same close and confirmation rule to all ten cases. Do not rename a failed breakout after seeing the eventual direction.
For a potential reversal, require the additional trigger specified by the chosen playbook (for example displacement and a selected structure break); the sweep itself is not an entry.
Record ambiguous cases as ambiguous rather than forcing a sweep/run label.
tutorials.deliverable: A ten-case classification sheet with screenshots, timestamps, reclaim/acceptance labels and separate trigger outcomes.
review: The reclaim/acceptance rule is fixed in advance.
A wick through a level is not automatically a reversal.
Ambiguous observations are retained.

tutorials.title: Measure FVGs, CE, IFVG and BPR
tutorials.objective: Measure three-candle FVGs and related imbalance concepts with exact boundaries and explicit invalidation rules.
materials: OHLC candles on one named timeframe
A calculator or chart measurement tool
A written wick/body mitigation rule
steps: Choose one timeframe and write down whether the data are time-based or trade-based. Use the candle highs/lows, not a drawn box alone.
For a bullish FVG, check whether candle 3 low is above candle 1 high; for a bearish FVG, check whether candle 3 high is below candle 1 low.
Record each gap's far edges and calculate its midpoint (CE) arithmetically. Do not assume the midpoint causes a reaction.
If studying IFVG, require the source/playbook's qualifying body close through the far edge. If studying BPR, confirm overlap of a bullish and bearish FVG.
Record wick touch, partial fill, full fill and invalidation separately. Do not mix a two-candle body imbalance with a three-candle FVG.
tutorials.deliverable: Ten candidate zones with candle OHLC, calculated boundaries/midpoint, mitigation state and at least two rejected/non-qualifying examples.
review: Three-candle boundaries are correct.
CE is calculated from the selected zone edges.
Wick touch and body-close invalidation are not conflated.

tutorials.title: Map Dealing Range, Premium/Discount and PD Arrays
tutorials.objective: Anchor one dealing range to a structural event, calculate equilibrium and map reference arrays without redrawing anchors.
materials: A completed chart with a clearly identified structural leg
A fixed swing-high/swing-low selection rule
A calculator or Fibonacci tool
steps: Identify the structural event that defines the range. Record timeframe, anchor high and anchor low before examining subsequent price action.
Calculate equilibrium as the arithmetic midpoint between the two chosen range extremes. Label above and below only after the range is fixed.
Mark relevant PD Arrays inside or around the range, such as FVGs, order blocks or breakers, and state the boundary convention used.
If using OTE or extensions, record the exact impulse anchors and the percentage convention. Treat these as practitioner references rather than statistical probabilities.
Record what would invalidate the range or array and when a new structural event is allowed to create a replacement range.
tutorials.deliverable: Five fixed dealing-range maps with the anchors, midpoint, premium/discount, arrays and invalidation rules visible.
review: Range anchors are justified by a structural event.
Equilibrium is exactly 50% of the selected range.
The range is not moved after the outcome is visible.

tutorials.title: Build a DST-Safe Session and Time-Anchor Plan
tutorials.objective: Apply session windows and time anchors using America/New_York and the correct exchange schedule.
materials: A timezone-aware chart or clock
The instrument's official trading-hours calendar
A completed chart spanning a DST change
steps: Set the reference timezone to America/New_York. Do not hard-code one IST offset for the whole year.
Verify the product session, maintenance break and holiday schedule on the official exchange source.
Mark the playbook's chosen session or anchor window only after writing down its start/end definition.
Carry the completed range high/low or open reference forward and record whether price rejects or accepts beyond it.
Keep a time window separate from direction: a killzone or Silver Bullet window does not create a setup without the required location and trigger.
tutorials.deliverable: A weekly session sheet in ET and converted IST with DST notes, product session source and three annotated completed sessions.
review: America/New_York is used as the reference zone.
IST conversions change with US DST.
Exchange open, ICT midnight open and broker day open remain distinct.

tutorials.title: Run a Cross-Market SMT Comparison
tutorials.objective: Compare related futures markets on synchronized swings and matched expiries, while treating SMT as a filter rather than a standalone trigger.
materials: Two or three related contracts with matched expiry conventions
Synchronized chart timezones and sessions
A dated comparison log
steps: Choose the pair/group in advance (for example NQ/ES/YM, 6E/6B/DX or GC/SI) and state whether the comparison is direct or inverse.
Match the session, swing timestamps and contract-expiry basis. Do not compare mismatched continuous-contract rolls.
Mark the same prior swing/reference on each market and record which market confirms or fails to confirm.
Label a divergence candidate only when the swing comparison is genuinely comparable. Check market-specific news or contract differences.
Wait for the execution market's own structure/trigger rule; do not enter solely because another market failed to make a new high/low.
tutorials.deliverable: Ten synchronized comparison examples, including confirming and non-confirming cases, with a separate trigger/invalidation field.
review: Same time window and expiry basis are used.
Inverse comparisons are handled explicitly.
SMT is not treated as a standalone entry signal.

tutorials.title: Replay an Entry Model Without Hindsight
tutorials.objective: Convert an ICT model into a checklist of context, trigger, entry, invalidation, target and no-trade conditions.
materials: One model definition from the supplied playbook
A completed replay chart and exact contract/timeframe
Risk calculator and trade journal
steps: Choose exactly one model and copy its prerequisites into a checklist before replay.
Mark the higher-timeframe context, relevant liquidity and session/time conditions before exposing the later candles.
Walk forward one bar at a time. Mark each prerequisite as pass, fail or unavailable. A missing requirement means the model is not qualified.
Only after qualification, write the exact entry, stop/invalidation, target and size assumptions. Include commission, fees and slippage in any later performance study.
Log both qualified and disqualified cases. Do not report win rate or expectancy from a hand-picked sample.
tutorials.deliverable: A 20-case model replay ledger with qualified/no-trade labels, rule version, costs assumption and screenshots.
review: All prerequisites are defined before replay.
No hindsight relabeling of the setup.
No performance claim without a reproducible test.

tutorials.title: Audit a Supplemental ICT/SMC Term
tutorials.objective: Research non-standard terminology without elevating community labels into canonical ICT rules.
materials: The existing source note and references for a selected concept
At least two source descriptions when available
A rule-definition sheet
steps: Start with the concept's evidence label and source note. Identify whether it is source-derived, supplemental, secondary or community terminology.
Open each cited source and record its author, date, wording and exact boundary/trigger definition. Do not treat search results as official lesson verification.
Compare definitions and list any disagreement. If no primary definition is available, retain the item as a research glossary note.
Write a measurable operational version with timeframe, price boundary, close/wick condition and invalidation—or mark it as not yet operational.
Only after the definition is stable should you collect examples for replay. Keep versions separate when source rules differ.
tutorials.deliverable: A source-comparison note with at least two reference entries where available, rule variants, uncertainty statement and a not-to-trade-until-defined decision.
review: Primary and secondary sources are distinguished.
Definition variants are preserved, not blended.
No unverified term is presented as an official signal.
